subject: Accounting
title: The AICPA Code of Conduct
description: One-minute skill: The AICPA Code of Conduct.

hook.text: The AICPA Code isn't just guidelines—it's the rulebook every U.S. CPA must follow or face consequences.

buildup.text: The American Institute of CPAs publishes a comprehensive code covering independence, integrity, and competence.

discovery.text: It includes principles (broad ideals) and rules (specific requirements) that govern professional behavior.

twist.text: Violating the code can result in suspension, loss of CPA license, or expulsion from the profession.

climax.text: The code evolves—new rules emerge after each major scandal to address newly exposed weaknesses.

punchline.text: The code adapts because the threats never stop changing.

quiz.question: What can happen if a CPA violates the AICPA Code of Conduct?
options: Loss of CPA license or expulsion from the profession

details.summary: The AICPA Code of Professional Conduct is the ethical framework governing CPAs in the United States. This topic covers its six core principles—responsibilities, public interest, integrity, objectivity, due care, and scope of service.
details.whyItMatters: The AICPA Code is the enforceable ethical standard for over 400,000 CPAs. Violations can result in loss of CPA certification and legal liability.
takeaways: The code is organized around six principles that guide all professional conduct
Rules are enforceable standards, while interpretations provide application guidance
Violations are investigated and can lead to suspension or revocation of CPA status

faq.question: What are the six principles of the AICPA Code of Conduct?
faq.answer: The six principles are: Responsibilities (to the profession), The Public Interest, Integrity, Objectivity and Independence, Due Care, and Scope and Nature of Services. Together they form the ethical foundation for all CPA activities in the U.S.

faq.question: What happens if a CPA violates the AICPA Code of Conduct?
faq.answer: The AICPA's Professional Ethics Division investigates complaints. Penalties range from required continuing education and public censure to suspension or revocation of AICPA membership, which may also affect state CPA license status.
